key_insight: RepWAM shifts world action modeling away from pixel-only reconstruction and toward semantic, representation-based visual-action tokenization. This helps the model learn instruction-following dynamics that better connect future prediction with robot control.
problem_solved: Existing world action models often use video tokenizers optimized for visual reconstruction, which preserve appearance but do not provide strong supervision for learning actionable, instruction-following behavior.
method: Builds a representation-centric world action model (RepWAM) instead of relying on reconstruction-oriented video tokenizers.
Introduces representation visual-action tokenizers that encode semantic visual-action latent structure, not just pixel fidelity.
Aligns future prediction with robot-control-relevant dynamics to improve actionable understanding of scenes and instructions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a more task-relevant way to train world models for robotics and embodied agents. It can improve how models generalize from observation to action by learning semantics that matter for control, not just reconstruction quality.
